draft.title: Shapes and polarity of molecules
card: Pairs of electrons around a central atom repel each other, so they spread as far apart as they can. This sets the shape of the molecule.
Two bonded atoms and no lone pairs on the centre give a linear shape, as in CO2. Four bonded atoms and no lone pairs give a tetrahedral shape, as in CH4.
Lone pairs also repel, so they bend the shape. Two bonded atoms and two lone pairs on the centre give a bent shape, as in H2O.
A bond is polar when atoms share electrons unevenly. A molecule is polar only if its polar bonds are arranged unevenly, so they do not cancel. CO2 has polar bonds but is non-polar. H2O is polar.
draft.remember: Electron pairs spread apart to set the shape. Polar bonds in an uneven shape make a polar molecule.

a.q: Why is a water molecule polar, while a carbon dioxide molecule is not?
opts: Water is bent, so its polar bonds do not cancel
Water has bonds, but carbon dioxide has none
Water has more atoms than carbon dioxide has
Carbon dioxide has bonds that share electrons evenly
a.why: Water is bent, so the pull of its two polar bonds does not cancel and one side of the molecule is more negative. Carbon dioxide does have polar bonds, but its linear shape makes them cancel, so the last option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about the shape of each molecule and whether the pulls cancel.

b.q: A methane molecule, CH4, has four identical bonds around the carbon atom with no lone pairs. Which describes its shape and polarity?
opts: Tetrahedral, and non-polar as the bond pulls cancel
Tetrahedral, and polar as its bonds are polar
Bent, and polar as the bond pulls do not cancel
Linear, and non-polar as it has identical bonds
b.why: Four bonded atoms with no lone pairs spread out into a tetrahedral shape. This shape is even, so the pulls of the bonds cancel and the molecule is non-polar. Calling it polar is tempting, but a molecule with an even shape is not polar just because its bonds are.
b.clue: Check the shape first, then ask if the bond pulls cancel.

a.best: Water is bent, so its polar bonds do not cancel

b.best: Tetrahedral, and non-polar as the bond pulls cancel
